patterns.reminder: NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables are bundled into browser code. Never put secret keys, service-role keys or LLM API keys in them.
This looks like a hardcoded secret key. Read it from a backend environment variable validated in apps/backend/src/env.ts.
Never trust supabase.auth.getSession() in server code. Use supabase.auth.getClaims(), or getUser() when a fresh user record is needed.
adminDb bypasses Row Level Security. Use withRls() for user-scoped queries; adminDb is only for migrations, seeds and apps/backend/src/jobs/**.

App data goes through the backend API (/api rewrite), not Next.js Server Actions. A Server Action is a public POST endpoint; if one is truly needed, it must validate input, authenticate and authorize like a backend route.
CORS must use the ALLOWED_ORIGINS allowlist, never '*'.
sql.raw() skips parameterisation. Use bound parameters; only whitelisted identifiers may ever be raw.
Disabling RLS exposes the table to every user through the Data API. Keep RLS enabled and write policies instead.
